title: PIM-MMU: A Memory Management Unit for Accelerating Data Transfers in Commercial PIM Systems
problem: DRAM↔PIM data transfers in commercial PIM systems like UPMEM suffer from high CPU utilization, high power consumption, and low read/write throughput, creating a critical bottleneck for memory-intensive workloads.
motivation: Commercial PIM systems provide high memory bandwidth for acceleration, but inefficient data transfers between DRAM and PIM address spaces severely limit overall performance and energy efficiency.
method: PIM-MMU implements a hardware/software co-design combining three synergistic components: a hardware-based data copy engine that offloads transfer operations from CPU, a PIM-optimized memory scheduler that improves access coordination, and a heterogeneity-aware memory mapping function that efficiently manages address translation. The software stack orchestrates these components for seamless operation.
key_novelty: Synergistic hardware/software co-design combining a dedicated data copy engine, optimized memory scheduler, and heterogeneity-aware mapping to eliminate DRAM↔PIM transfer bottlenecks in commercial PIM systems.
contributions: In-depth characterization of UPMEM PIM system identifying critical DRAM↔PIM transfer bottlenecks
Hardware-based data copy engine for offloading CPU-intensive transfer operations
PIM-optimized memory scheduler and heterogeneity-aware memory mapping function
4.1x throughput improvement and 4.1x energy-efficiency gain with 2.2x end-to-end speedup on real-world workloads
